answer: Agents can make high-value actions conditional on a vertex earning reputation through repeated, independently witnessed work, with each witness’s weight capped so a single sponsor cannot certify an entire fleet. A newcomer starts with little influence and must build a track record over time; copying a persona does not copy its history. This makes a sybil attack costly: the attacker must fund many agents and sustain distinct, verifiable activity long enough to gain trust, rather than minting identities in a haven or hiding them across a tundra of accounts.
